subject: Compact inspector: correlation tile for high-cardinality anomalies
messages:
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: bethany.lin@acme.com
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Compact inspector: correlation tile for high-cardinality anomalies

Team —

Quick ask from my side after a sync with ACME: they want a smaller console tile that surfaces correlated signals across cost/latency/percentile spikes for a given route slice (customer+path). The goal is a compact, single-row inspector that shows:
- top 3 correlated routes (by cost delta)
- representative tail latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
- a short timeline sparkline with anomaly markers
- link-to-trace and link-to-tenant-drill

Why compact: ACME wants a button on their internal daily ops dashboard (small real estate). We need this to be pre-aggregated (or at least fast enough) so it can load under 500ms for a dashboard row.

Initial questions:
1) Is it feasible to produce this as a pre-computed tile (daily + 15m refresh) vs live compute?
2) What sampling / prefixing strategy would keep cost acceptable while preserving correlation signal?
3) Any red flags from infra on query volumes if we expose link-to-trace at click time?

I've attached a rough mockup (compact_inspector_mockup_v2.pdf) and a small sample of the sampling/latency matrix ACME shared.

If we can scope an MVP (pre-aggregated with 15m refresh + on-click live trace link) I think we can deliver within a single sprint with a follow-up for live mode.

Thanks — pinging Marcus for perf constraints and Grace for UX/dev breakdown.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions PM, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, bethany.lin@acme.com
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compact inspector: correlation tile for high-cardinality anomalies

Sergio —

Thanks for the context and mockup. High level thoughts: pre-aggregation looks like the right starting point to meet the <500ms target, but we need to be explicit about the time window and cardinality ceilings. Two quick items I want us to agree on before design/implementation:

1) Cardinality cap: Are we capping to top-N customers/routes per tenant (e.g., top 10 routes by token volume) or using a dynamic sampling lottery? Top-N will be much cheaper.
2) Refresh cadence: 15m is doable if we run incremental jobs and keep only deltas; 5m would double cost.

Operationally, the biggest infra risk is on-demand expanded queries when clicking "link-to-trace" for many tiles simultaneously. We should gate the link behind a throttled request and/or pre-warm a small trace cache for customers on Dedicated.

I can sketch the pre-agg pipeline: daily full + 15m incremental that writes compact rows to the telemetry store. That lets the console read a single document per tile. I'll follow up with a rough cost calc if we choose top-N by tokens.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, bethany.lin@acme.com
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compact inspector: correlation tile for high-cardinality anomalies

Looping in a quick UX/dev take after reviewing the mockup. Mockup link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xMockupExample/view?usp=sharing

Implementation notes:
- UI: compact row should be ~48px height. Use condensed sparklines and 3-chip list for correlated routes. On hover, expand to show p50/p95/p99 details.
- Data contract: the tile should return a single JSON with fields {route_key, corr_routes[3], p50, p95, p99, sparkline(20), trace_url}. Keep payload <4KB.
- Sampling: start with top-10 by token volume per tenant. If tile misses signal in customer QA, we can enable 'adaptive-sampling' which uses a flagged minor job to surface additional candidates.

Questions for Marcus: does the pre-agg pipeline support writing the compact row as a single document keyed by tenant+route slice? If yes, we can avoid multiple read requests on render.

I added a short spreadsheet (sampling-latency-matrix.csv) that approximates the compute cost under top-10 and adaptive sampling. The adaptive column increases CPU by ~35% for worst-case tenants.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Designer, Console ==> Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: bethany.lin@acme.com
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 15:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compact inspector: correlation tile for high-cardinality anomalies

Thanks all — short decision + next steps to keep this actionable: 

Decisions: 
- MVP approach: pre-aggregated compact row; top-10 routes by token volume; 15m incremental refresh.
- UI payload constraint: keep under 4KB, single document per tile keyed by tenant+route slice.
- Traces: link-to-trace will be throttled (10 concurrent per-tenant) and fall back to a gated request (request queued + email when ready) for high concurrency.

Action items: 
- Marcus: create OBS-1423 with the pipeline template and rough cost estimate by EOD Wednesday (assigned). (link: https://redwoodcorp.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-1423)
- Grace: finalize compact mockup and hand off CSS tokens + interaction spec (ETA next Tue). Attached mockup_v2 included.
- Sergio: confirm ACME acceptance criteria and add to the ticket (I'll loop Bethany for signoff).

If we stick to this scope, PM estimate: 1 sprint (prod infra + UI), plus a follow-on improvement for adaptive sampling. I'll flag for next sprint planning.

— Irene Choi
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
